'''Zachary LaVine''' (born March 10, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He grew up in [[Washington (state)|Washington]], where he was honored as the state's top high school player. In his first year with UCLA in 2013–14, he was named one of the top freshman in the [[Pacific-12 Conference]].  Following his freshman season, LaVine declared his eligibility for the [[2014 NBA draft]].

==Early life==
LaVine was born in [[Renton, Washington]], to athletic parents. His father, Paul, played [[American football]] professionally in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) and [[National Football League]] (NFL), and his mother, CJ, was a [[softball]] player.<ref name=ucla_bio/><ref>{{cite news|last=Kelley|first=Mason|title=Bothell's Zach LaVine shoots for the top|date=November 30, 2011|newspaper=The Seattle Times|url=http://seattletimes.com/html/highschoolsports/2016900848_mason01.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6NicdTxxD|archivedate=February 28, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> LaVine attended [[Bothell High School]] in [[Bothell, Washington]].<ref name=ucla_bio>{{cite web|title=Zach LaVine bio|work=UCLABruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=208601163|accessdate=February 27, 2014}}</ref> Playing [[point guard]], he was their primary ball handler.<ref name=mays_02272014>{{cite news|last=Mays|first=Robert|title=Swinging on the NBA Draft Yo-Yo|date=February 27, 2014|work=Grantland.com|url=http://grantland.com/features/swinging-on-the-nba-draft-yo-yo/|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6Ni2Sh8DH|archivedate=February 27, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> In his senior year, he averaged 28.5 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, and was named the 2013 [[Associated Press]] Washington state player of the year and [[Washington Mr. Basketball]];<ref name=ucla_bio/> however, he only received limited national recognition.<ref name=mays_02272014/>

==College==
On June 20, 2012, LaVine verbally committed to attending UCLA and playing for coach [[Ben Howland]] for the 2013 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bruinsnation.com/2012/6/21/3106788/zach-lavine-ucla-basketballs-first-2013-commitment|title=Zach LaVine - UCLA Basketball's First 2013 Commitment|date=Jun 21, 2012|accessdate=Feb 19, 2014}}</ref> After Howland was fired nine months later, LaVine considered staying in-state and attending the [[University of Washington]] instead.  However, he decided to remain with UCLA and their new coach, [[Steve Alford]]; LaVine had inherited an affection for UCLA from his father, who grew up a fan of Bruins basketball while growing up in nearby [[San Bernadino, California]].<ref name=wang_03052014>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=UCLA basketball notes: Zach LaVine shaking off slump in time for Washington homecoming|date=March 5, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20140305/ucla-basketball-notes-zach-lavine-shaking-off-slump-in-time-for-washington-homecoming|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6NuFztrrL|archivedate=March 7, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref>

After a strong start to [[2013–14 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2013–14]] as the team's [[sixth man]], featuring an impressive display of outside shooting and explosive [[slam dunk|dunk]]s, the former point guard LaVine evoked memories of UCLA alumnus [[Russell Westbrook]]'s beginnings.<ref name=mays_02272014/> [[NBA draft]] pundits began ranking LaVine high on their projections for the [[2014 NBA Draft]] if he [[NBA draft declaration|declared himself eligible]].<ref name=mays_02272014/><ref>[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-basketball/news/20131220/ucla-zach-lavine-nba-steve-alford-dunk/ UCLA's Zach LaVine is dunking his way to the NBA]</ref>  [[ESPN.com]] draft expert [[Chad Ford]] attributed LaVine's appeal to the Westbrook comparisons. At one point, Ford listed him as the 10th overall pick, while NBADraft.net ranked him fifth.<ref name=mays_02272014/> During the season, LaVine typically entered the game with Bryce Alford, who usually handled the ball, while starter [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]] was the team's main facilitator.<ref name=mays_02272014/> During a six-game span beginning on January 26, 2014, he endured a shooting slump where he made just 7 of 36 shots from the field.<ref name=wang_03052014/>  He averaged 9.4 points per game during the season, but did not reach double-figures in 14 of the final 18 games.<ref>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=UCLA freshman Zach LaVine to declare for NBA draft|date=March 28, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/20140328/ucla-freshman-zach-lavine-to-declare-for-nba-draft|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6OQQ5EF4u|archivedate=March 28, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> In the final five games, he scored just 11 points and was 0 for 8 on [[three-point field goal|three-point attempts]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=UCLA men’s basketball gains and losses in Steve Alford’s first season|date=April 3, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20140403/ucla-mens-basketball-gains-and-losses-in-steve-alfords-first-season|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6OZ8izwu4|archivedate=April 3, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> Despite his late-season struggles, he was named to the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kartje|first=Ryan|title=Anderson, Adams named to All-Pac-12 first team|date=March 10, 2014|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=http://www.ocregister.com/ucla/pac-604926-team-named.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6O0JLLoYE|archivedate=March 11, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|title=2013-14 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 10, 2014|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2014/03/10/2013-14-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6Nz8ZWOJl|archivedate=March 11, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref>

On April 16, 2014, he announced that he will forego his remaining collegiate eligibility and enter the 2014 NBA Draft.<ref>[http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=209468106 UCLA's Zach LaVine Declares for NBA Draft ], UCLABruins.com, April 16, 2014</ref> At the team's annual banquet, he was given the Seymour Armond Memorial Award as one of the team’s most valuable freshmen.
